text:
alex_support: Seeing a spike of 429s for multiple customers starting ~10:12 UTC. Root cause looks like regional capacity exhaustion in us-west and automatic spillover to eu-west — which then hit queueing and propagated 502/504 timeouts. Customers complaining about cross-region latency and some flagged data residency concerns.

maya_oncall: Confirmed. Alerts showed us-west GPU pool at 100% and queue length growing. Spillover policy kicked in and redirected ~40% of queued requests to eu-west around 10:14 UTC. eu-west then started returning 503/timeout from long tails.

chris_eng: Any specific model or instance type dominating? I see a big surge on gpt-x-large on us-west nodes. Example request id: req_8f3a2b7c — logs: ```ERR 429 capacity_exhausted region=us-west pool=reserved model=gpt-x-large fallback=eu-west```

alex_support: A few paying customers hit rate limits even though they have dedicated capacity. One report says they still got routed to eu-west despite account being labeled "dedicated-us-west". That's the main escalation from support — customer expects isolation.

sre-bot: Incident detected: region_capacity_exhaustion(us-west) threshold=0.98 -> spillover_enabled. Auto-mitigation: route_to_fallback(eu-west) applied.

liz_prod: This is concerning — dedicated capacity should never spill to another region. Product control plane should respect "dedicated" flag. Can we repro?

ram_devex: Repro steps I used in staging (simulating queue backlog): 1) POST /v1/generate with header `X-Region: us-west` 2) throttle background workers until pool saturated 3) observe `x-served-region: eu-west` in response headers and increased latency >= 3200ms. Example curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Region: us-west" -d '{"model":"gpt-x-large","input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```

chris_eng: Found the route decision log for account acct-998: ```route_decision ts=2026-03-12T10:14:21Z account=acct-998 src=us-west decision=spillover target=eu-west reason=capacity_exhausted bypass_dedicated=false```. Looks like bypass_dedicated flag was false in the log (bad), so the routing layer ignored dedicated isolation. That's a config bug.

maya_oncall: Short-term mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable cross-region spillover (global kill-switch) 2) increase us-west pool by spinning up warm nodes 3) set per-account rule to block fallback for dedicated accounts. Which do we want now?

ops_billing: Note: some accounts noticed egress billing in eu-west which they did not expect. If we serve in another region we should flag and bill correctly or refund. Ops will need a list of affected request IDs to reconcile.

chris_eng: I'll roll a patch to respect dedicated flag in routing decision and add an extra check to prevent spillover for accounts with isolation labels. Will try to push a hotfix in the next 22 minutes; need SRE approval to deploy to prod.

ram_devex: For support replies, recommend messaging: "We identified an automatic spillover due to temporary capacity exhaustion in your chosen region. We have disabled cross-region spillover for dedicated accounts and are rolling back the affected requests. We will also review billing for any cross-region usage."

maya_oncall: Deploying patch-now on canary (eng-runtime/canary). If rollout looks good for 5 minutes we'll promote to prod. Meanwhile I'll disable global spillover as a nail-in-the-coffin mitigation (toggle -> OFF).

alex_support: Customer-facing update prepared and sent to 3 affected customers. Included apology, mitigation steps, and offer to review billing. Collecting logs/req ids.

chris_eng: Canary patch stable. Will promote in 3m. After deploy we should validate: 1) dedicated accounts never get `x-served-region` != requested region 2) no new 429s introduced. Please paste quick smoke test results here.

maya_oncall: Post-deploy quick checks: canary/us-west pool CPU ok, spillover toggle OFF, no more route_decision entries with bypass_dedicated=true. Rolling to prod now.

ops_billing: Will ingest list from alex_support — need request ids for 10:12-10:30 window. We'll prepare any credits/refunds if warranted.

alex_support: Pushed list. Closing thread once billing confirms reconciliations and product confirms root cause fix in prod. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
